methodological_questions: How to measure opponents H2-H1 change?
Reliability estimation (split-half, intraclass correlation) for team-season metric
Variance decomposition of defensive effect across halves
Confounding by game script, blowouts, garbage time
Regression to mean when selecting extreme half performances
Adequacy of 120 team-seasons for detecting stable defensive trait
Isolating defensive from offensive influence on opponent scoring change
evidence_does_not_establish: No prior research on this specific question was available in the retrieved records, so nothing has been established or ruled out by earlier project work.
own_inferences: The quantity 'opponent H2-H1 change' can be derived from play-by-play data, and its stability across games and seasons can be estimated via intraclass correlation or hierarchical modeling.

The primary challenges are: (1) the change score inherits regression-to-the-mean artifacts because first-half opponent scoring is a noisy baseline; (2) second-half scoring is confounded by game script (blowouts, garbage time, opponent resting starters); (3) with only 30 teams observed over 4 seasons, power to detect a modest team-level variance component is limited.
Without controlling for first-half performance and game context, any apparent reliability in raw H2-H1 differences would be suspect.
uncertainties: The true size of a defensive halftime-adjustment trait, if it exists, is unknown; it may be so small that the available sample cannot distinguish it from noise.
How much of the second-half scoring change is attributable to the opponent's own offensive quality versus the defense's adjustment is difficult to isolate observationally.

historical_effect.explanation: No historical evidence was retrieved; the decision rests solely on the methodological assessment of the question with the available data.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 30 teams over 4 seasons; detecting a small between-team variance in halftime-adjustment effect likely requires a larger number of independent team observations or longer time series.
The H2-H1 change score is mechanically correlated with the first-half opponent scoring baseline, creating regression-to-the-mean artifacts unless the baseline is properly conditioned on.
Game script (point differential at halftime, garbage time, opponent resting patterns) strongly influences second-half scoring, potentially swamping the defensive signal.

prior_work.summary: No earlier project studies on this exact question were found; the question remains open.

risks.text: With 30 teams and 4 seasons, power to detect a small intraclass correlation for a defensive-adjustment trait may be low.
The raw H2-H1 opponent scoring difference is negatively correlated with first-half opponent scoring, a classic regression-to-the-mean pattern that can create spurious stability if not modeled.
Second-half opponent scoring is heavily influenced by game situation (blowouts, garbage time, opponent tactical shifts) that are not purely a function of the defense.
Per-game opponent half-to-half scoring changes are noisy, and aggregating over only a season per team may yield an unreliable metric, attenuating any between-team correlation.
When a defense already holds an opponent to very low scoring in the first half, the scoring change may be bounded on the low side (floor effect), distorting the distribution.

design.estimand: The team-specific, season-level causal effect of a defense on opponent second-half points per possession (PPP) relative to first-half PPP, after controlling for opponent offensive strength and game script; the stability (intraclass correlation, ICC) of this effect across half-season splits and across seasons.
design.unit: Defensive team-season, with within-season half-splits for reliability estimation; game-level data is used to estimate the team-season adjustment parameter.
design.sample: All regular-season games from the 2022-23 through 2025-26 seasons. Garbage-time minutes (defined as segments where score differential exceeds 20 points and quarter ≥ 4) are excluded. Fourth quarters of games with a point differential > 20 at the start of the quarter are also removed. Only games with both teams having at least 20 possessions in each half after garbage-time removal are retained.
design.power: Power will be assessed by simulation: using a hierarchical model with plausible effect sizes (e.g., team-level standard deviation in adjustment effect of 0.02–0.05 PPP) and the observed number of games per team-season, determine the minimum detectable ICC with 80% power at alpha = 0.05. If power is inadequate, at least three full seasons (2023-24 onward) will be used to extend the time series.
design.controls: Fixed effects: opponent season-long offensive rating (ORtg), home/away indicator, rest advantage (back-to-back indicator for both teams), point differential at halftime, half-level pace (estimated possessions), an indicator for whether the opponent's star players are available (derived from rotation data). The defense team-season random intercept will be the primary quantity.
design.falsification: 1. Compute the same H2-H1 defensive trait for offenses (team's own scoring change) and test whether it shows similar reliability; if it does, the trait may reflect general game-script artifacts rather than pure defense. 2. Shuffle games across teams within season and re-estimate ICC; reliability should vanish. 3. Split the season into first half and second half (by game date) and compare—large discrepancy would indicate non-stationarity (coaching changes, trades). 4. Check whether the team random effect is stable when using only first-half opponent PPP as outcome; it should be, but the adjustment effect should be orthogonal.
design.multiplicity: Only one primary hypothesis (ICC > 0) will be tested; any sensitivity analyses using alternative specifications will be labeled exploratory and corrected with Bonferroni.
design.decision_rule: A Bayesian hierarchical model (team random intercepts with partial pooling) will be fit. The hypothesis is supported if the 95% credible interval for the intraclass correlation (posterior of σ_team^2 / (σ_team^2 + σ_resid^2)) excludes zero and the posterior probability of σ_team > 0 exceeds 0.975. The study will conclude 'rejected' if the 90% credible interval for ICC is entirely below a pre-specified smallest effect size of interest (e.g., ICC = 0.05) and the posterior median is near zero.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular season play-by-play, substitution, and matchup data as available on 2026-10-06.
